title: Evaluate a periodic function using the period
stem: A function f is periodic with period 12. For which of the following expressions is it NOT guaranteed that the expression equals f(x) for all x?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: A shift of 24 is two full periods, so f(x + 24) = f(x) for all x.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: a shift by any whole number of periods leaves f unchanged: 24 = 2·12, −36 = −3·12 and 60 = 5·12, but 6 is half a period.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: A shift of −36 is three full periods backward, so f(x − 36) = f(x) for all x.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: A shift of 60 is five full periods, so f(x + 60) = f(x) for all x.

title: Evaluate a periodic function using the period (variant 1)
stem: A function g is periodic with period 5. For which of the following expressions is it NOT guaranteed that the expression equals g(x) for all x?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: A shift of 15 is three full periods, so g(x + 15) = g(x) for all x.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: 15 = 3·5, −10 = −2·5 and 50 = 10·5 are whole numbers of periods, but 12.5 = 2.5 periods.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: A shift of −10 is two full periods backward, so g(x − 10) = g(x) for all x.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: A shift of 50 is ten full periods, so g(x + 50) = g(x) for all x.

title: Evaluate a periodic function using the period (variant 2)
stem: A function h is periodic with period 8. For which of the following expressions is it NOT guaranteed that the expression equals h(x) for all x?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: A shift of 16 is two full periods, so h(x + 16) = h(x) for all x.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: A shift of −24 is three full periods backward, so h(x − 24) = h(x) for all x.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: A shift of 40 is five full periods, so h(x + 40) = h(x) for all x.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: 16 = 2·8, −24 = −3·8 and 40 = 5·8 are whole numbers of periods, but 20 = 2.5 periods.

title: Evaluate a periodic function using the period (variant 3)
stem: A function p is periodic with period 7. For which of the following expressions is it NOT guaranteed that the expression equals p(x) for all x?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: 49 = 7·7, −21 = −3·7 and 35 = 5·7 are whole numbers of periods, but 10 is not a multiple of 7.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: A shift of 49 is seven full periods, so p(x + 49) = p(x) for all x.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: A shift of −21 is three full periods backward, so p(x − 21) = p(x) for all x.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: A shift of 35 is five full periods, so p(x + 35) = p(x) for all x.

title: Average rates of change of a periodic function
stem: The height h(t), in meters, of the tide at a harbor is periodic with period 12 hours. High tide is h(0) = 2.4 and low tide is h(6) = 0.4, and the tide falls steadily from t = 0 to t = 6 and rises from t = 6 to t = 12. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average rate of change on [0, 6] is −1/3 meters per hour, and on [0, 12] it is +1/3 meters per hour.
choices.rationale: After a full period the height returns to its starting value, so the net change is 0 and not positive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average rate of change on [0, 6] is −2 meters per hour, and on [0, 12] it is 0 meters per hour.
choices.rationale: The change in height is −2 meters, and dividing by the length 6 hours gives −1/3, not −2.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average rate of change on [0, 6] is −1/3 meters per hour, and on [0, 12] it is 0 meters per hour.
choices.rationale: Correct: (0.4 − 2.4)/6 = −1/3; over a full period h(12) = h(0), so the average rate on [0, 12] is 0.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The average rate of change is 0 meters per hour on both [0, 6] and [0, 12], because the tide is periodic.
choices.rationale: A periodic function has average rate 0 over a full period only, and the tide changes from 2.4 to 0.4 on [0, 6].

title: Average rates of change of a periodic function (variant 1)
stem: A Ferris wheel rider's height h(t), in meters, is periodic with period 20 seconds. The rider is lowest at h(0) = 1 and highest at h(10) = 41. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average rate of change on [0, 10] is +4 meters per second, and on [0, 20] it is 0 meters per second.
choices.rationale: Correct: (41 − 1)/10 = 4 on [0, 10]; h(20) = h(0), so the average rate on [0, 20] is 0.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average rate of change on [0, 10] is +40 meters per second, and on [0, 20] it is 0 meters per second.
choices.rationale: 40 is the change in height, and the average rate divides it by the 10 seconds elapsed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average rate of change on [0, 10] is +4 meters per second, and on [0, 20] it is +2 meters per second.
choices.rationale: After one full period the rider is back at height 1, so the net change is 0, not 40 or 20.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The average rate of change is 0 meters per second on [0, 10] and +4 meters per second on [0, 20].
choices.rationale: This reverses the two intervals; the rider rises on [0, 10] and has no net change over a full period.

title: Average rates of change of a periodic function (variant 2)
stem: The temperature T(t) at a weather station is modeled by a sinusoidal function with period 24 hours. T has its maximum at t = 0 and its minimum at t = 12, and T is decreasing and concave down on the interval (0, 6). Which statement describes T on the interval (6, 12)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: T is increasing and concave up.
choices.rationale: T keeps decreasing until the minimum at t = 12, so it is not increasing on (6, 12).

choices.label: B
choices.text: T is decreasing and concave up.
choices.rationale: Correct: a sinusoid falls from its maximum to its minimum on (0, 12), bending down until the midline crossing at t = 6, then bending up toward the minimum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: T is decreasing and concave down.
choices.rationale: The concavity changes at the midline crossing t = 6, so it does not stay concave down.

choices.label: D
choices.text: T is increasing and concave down.
choices.rationale: T is not increasing before the minimum, and the concavity has changed to concave up.

title: Average rates of change of a periodic function (variant 3)
stem: An insect population g(t), in thousands, is periodic with period 3 years. The population has a maximum of 5 at t = 1 and a minimum of 1 at t = 2.5. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: g(10) = 1, because 10 is a whole number of years after the minimum at 2.5.
choices.rationale: The minima occur at 2.5 + 3k, and 10 is not of that form.

choices.label: B
choices.text: g(10) = 5, because the maximum occurs every year.
choices.rationale: The maximum occurs once per period of 3 years, not every year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: g(10) cannot be determined, because 10 lies outside the given data.
choices.rationale: A periodic function is determined everywhere by its values on one period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: g(10) = 5, because 10 = 1 + 3(3), a whole number of periods after the first maximum.
choices.rationale: Correct: maxima occur at t = 1 + 3k, and 10 = 1 + 9.

title: Signs and quadrants from one trigonometric value
stem: An angle θ is in Quadrant III, and cos θ = −5/13. Which choice gives sin θ and tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Sine is negative in Quadrant III, and a positive sine would place the angle in Quadrant II.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: The quotient of two negative numbers is positive, so tan θ is positive in Quadrant III.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: sin θ = −√(1 − 25/169) = −12/13 in Quadrant III, and tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = (−12/13)/(−5/13) = 12/5.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio, giving cos θ/sin θ instead of sin θ/cos θ.

title: Signs and quadrants from one trigonometric value (variant 1)
stem: An angle θ is in Quadrant II, and sin θ = 3/5. Which choice gives cos θ and tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: cos θ = −√(1 − 9/25) = −4/5 in Quadrant II, and tan θ = (3/5)/(−4/5) = −3/4.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Cosine is negative in Quadrant II, and a positive cosine would place the angle in Quadrant I.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Tangent is negative in Quadrant II because sine is positive and cosine is negative.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio, giving cos θ/sin θ in magnitude instead of sin θ/cos θ.

title: Signs and quadrants from one trigonometric value (variant 2)
stem: An angle θ is in Quadrant IV, and tan θ = −2. Which choice gives sin θ and cos θ?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: These signs place the angle in Quadrant II, where sine is positive and cosine is negative.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This swaps the two values, so tan θ would be −1/2 instead of −2.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: These signs place the angle in Quadrant III, where both are negative and the tangent is positive.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = −2 with cos θ > 0 and sin θ < 0 in Quadrant IV; with sin² + cos² = 1 we get cos θ = 1/√5 and sin θ = −2/√5.

title: Signs and quadrants from one trigonometric value (variant 3)
stem: An angle θ satisfies sin θ = −8/17 and cos θ > 0. What is tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Sine is negative and cosine is positive, so the tangent is negative, and a positive value ignores the sign of sine.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio, giving cos θ/sin θ instead of sin θ/cos θ.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This both inverts the ratio and drops the sign.

title: Ratios from a point not on the unit circle
stem: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through the point (−6, 8). Which choice gives sin θ, cos θ and tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: sin θ = 8, cos θ = −6, tan θ = −4/3
choices.rationale: Sine and cosine are the y and x coordinates only on the unit circle, and these must be divided by r = 10.

choices.label: B
choices.text: sin θ = 4/5, cos θ = −3/5, tan θ = −4/3

choices.label: C
choices.text: sin θ = 4/5, cos θ = 3/5, tan θ = −4/3
choices.rationale: The x-coordinate is negative, so cosine is negative in Quadrant II.

choices.label: D
choices.text: sin θ = 4/5, cos θ = −3/5, tan θ = −3/4
choices.rationale: Tangent is y/x = 8/(−6), which is the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, not x/y.

title: Ratios from a point not on the unit circle (variant 1)
stem: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through the point (5, −12). Which choice gives sin θ, cos θ and tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: sin θ = −12, cos θ = 5, tan θ = −12/5
choices.rationale: Sine and cosine are the y and x coordinates only on the unit circle, and these must be divided by r = 13.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: The y-coordinate is negative, so sine is negative in Quadrant IV.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Tangent is y/x = −12/5, which is the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, not x/y.

title: Ratios from a point not on the unit circle (variant 2)
stem: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through the point (−4, −3). Which choice gives sin θ, cos θ and tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: sin θ = −3/5, cos θ = −4/5, tan θ = 3/4

choices.label: B
choices.text: sin θ = −3, cos θ = −4, tan θ = 3/4
choices.rationale: Sine and cosine are the y and x coordinates only on the unit circle, and these must be divided by r = 5.

choices.label: C
choices.text: sin θ = −3/5, cos θ = −4/5, tan θ = −3/4
choices.rationale: The quotient of two negative numbers is positive, so tan θ is positive in Quadrant III.

choices.label: D
choices.text: sin θ = −3/5, cos θ = −4/5, tan θ = 4/3
choices.rationale: Tangent is y/x = 3/4, which is the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, not x/y.

title: Ratios from a point not on the unit circle (variant 3)
stem: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through the point (−8, −15). Which choice gives sin θ, cos θ and tan θ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: sin θ = −15, cos θ = −8, tan θ = 15/8
choices.rationale: Sine and cosine are the y and x coordinates only on the unit circle, and these must be divided by r = 17.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: The quotient of two negative numbers is positive, so tan θ is positive in Quadrant III.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Tangent is y/x = 15/8, which is the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, the ratio of the y-coordinate to the x-coordinate, not x/y.

title: Solve for angles from a sine or cosine value
stem: Which angles θ in the interval [0, 2π) satisfy sin θ = −√3/2?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: These angles have sin θ = +√3/2, since they lie in Quadrants I and II.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 2π/3 is in Quadrant II, where sine is positive, so it cannot be a solution.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: the reference angle is π/3 and sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV, so θ = π + π/3 = 4π/3 and θ = 2π − π/3 = 5π/3.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: These have reference angle π/6, for which the sine is −1/2 and not −√3/2.

title: Solve for angles from a sine or cosine value (variant 1)
stem: Which angles θ in the interval [0, 2π) satisfy cos θ = −√2/2?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: the reference angle is π/4 and cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III, so θ = 3π/4 and θ = 5π/4.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: These angles have cos θ = +√2/2, since they lie in Quadrants I and IV.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 7π/4 is in Quadrant IV, where cosine is positive, so it cannot be a solution.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Π/4 is in Quadrant I, where cosine is positive, so it cannot be a solution.

title: Solve for angles from a sine or cosine value (variant 2)
stem: On the interval [0, 2π), sin θ = 1/2 and cos θ < 0. What is θ?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Π/6 has sin θ = 1/2, but its cosine is positive, so it fails the second condition.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 7π/6 has cosine negative but sine −1/2, so it fails the first condition.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 11π/6 has sine −1/2 and cosine positive, so it fails both conditions.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: sin θ = 1/2 gives π/6 and 5π/6; cosine is negative only in Quadrant II, so θ = 5π/6.

title: Solve for angles from a sine or cosine value (variant 3)
stem: How many solutions does the equation cos θ = 1/2 have on the interval [0, 4π)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This counts only the solutions on one revolution, but the interval covers two.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: on [0, 2π) the solutions are π/3 and 5π/3, and adding 2π gives 7π/3 and 11π/3, for 4 in total.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: The solutions come in pairs, one in Quadrant I and one in Quadrant IV on each revolution, so an odd count is impossible.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: There are exactly two solutions per revolution, not three.

title: Symmetry and shift identities
stem: Let θ be an angle with 0 < θ < π/2 and sin θ = 3/5. What is the value of cos(θ + π)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Adding π reverses the direction of the point on the unit circle, so the cosine changes sign.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Cos(θ + π) is −cos θ, which is not −sin θ.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Cos(θ + π) is the negative of cos θ, so it is not sin θ.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: cos θ = 4/5 in Quadrant I, and cos(θ + π) = −cos θ = −4/5.

title: Symmetry and shift identities (variant 1)
stem: Let θ be an angle in Quadrant II with cos θ = −5/13. What is the value of sin(π − θ)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Sin(π − θ) equals sin θ, and sine is positive in Quadrant II, so it is not negative.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This is −cos θ, which is the value of cos(π − θ), not of sin(π − θ).

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is cos θ itself, but the question asks for a sine.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: sin θ = 12/13 in Quadrant II, and sin(π − θ) = sin θ = 12/13.

title: Symmetry and shift identities (variant 2)
stem: Let θ be an angle in Quadrant III with sin θ = −4/5. What is the value of cos(θ − π)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: cos θ = −3/5 in Quadrant III, and cos(θ − π) = −cos θ = 3/5.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This is cos θ itself, but shifting by π changes the sign.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is −sin θ, and it is not the cosine of the shifted angle.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This is sin θ itself, and the question asks for a cosine.

title: Symmetry and shift identities (variant 3)
stem: Let θ be an angle in Quadrant IV with cos θ = 4/5. What is the value of sin(−θ)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This is sin θ itself, but reflecting the angle changes the sign of sine.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: sin θ = −3/5 in Quadrant IV, and sin(−θ) = −sin θ = 3/5.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is cos θ, and cos(−θ) = cos θ, not sin(−θ).

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This is −cos θ, which does not equal sin(−θ).
